name: The Christopher Diagnosis Vision (March 1974)
date_basis: Exegesis; Tessa Dick's testimony; medical record subsequent
summary: PKD reports being told (by the AI Voice / pink beam transmission) that his infant son Christopher has an inguinal hernia; subsequent medical examination confirms the diagnosis. The episode is one of the few theophanies with external corroboration.
description: In March 1974, during the period of pink-beam transmissions, PKD reports being told that his infant son Christopher (born July 1973) has an undiagnosed medical condition — variously narrated as an inguinal hernia, a hydrocele, or a strangulated organ — that requires surgery. Tessa Dick's memoir *The Owl in Daylight* (2009) confirms that Christopher was taken to the doctor on PKD's insistence and that a hernia was found. This is one of the very few PKD theophanies with external Lane-D corroboration; even skeptical biographers (Sutin, Arnold) record the medical confirmation as fact.

pkd_interpretations.interpretation: The transmitter knew about Christopher's condition before any human did; this is the strongest external evidence that the transmission is real.
Possibly Tessa or I had subconsciously observed the hernia symptoms and the 'transmission' is the unconscious surfacing as conscious gnosis.

scholar_interpretations.interpretation: Sutin records the Christopher diagnosis as the strongest evidential anchor for the 2-3-74 cluster.
Tessa attests to the medical diagnosis and to PKD's insistence on the urgency before the doctor confirmed it.
Arnold acknowledges the diagnosis but suggests the 'foreknowledge' is reconstructed retrospectively from ordinary parental observation.

primary_sources.excerpt: Tessa Dick's memoir confirms the medical diagnosis.
Multiple Exegesis segments return to Christopher as evidence.

contradiction_zone: no — the medical fact is settled; only the foreknowledge interpretation is contested
pkd_doubt_evidence: PKD himself entertains the subliminal-observation reading.
